top_categories.workout_context: 52ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Surrey Rumble. Train it until it feels boring.
At mile 60 of 80, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Surrey Rumble's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before March.
At Surrey Rumble, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
Surrey Rumble's mixed terrain forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 80 miles.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 80 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 4,167ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
Varied gradients on mixed terrain demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 80 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Tempo is Surrey Rumble's race pace. The wattage you'll hold for 80 miles on mixed terrain. Train it until it's automatic.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Surrey Rumble’s 80 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, G Spot, and Durability to prepare you for 80 miles of mixed terrain in Cobham, Surrey, England.
